activity_context.topic_title: Expressing Rational Functions as Sums of Partial Fractions

feedback.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$ and $B$ such that

$$
\frac{4x+23}{(5-2x)(x+3)}=\frac{A}{5-2x}+\frac{B}{x+3}.
$$

Multiplying both sides by $(5-2x)(x+3)$ gives

$$
4x+23=A(x+3)+B(5-2x).
$$

For $x=-3$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4(-3)+23 & =A(-3+3)+B(5-2(-3)) \\ 11 & =11B \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=\frac{5}{2},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4(\frac{5}{2})+23 & =A(\frac{5}{2}+3)+B(5-2(\frac{5}{2})) \\ 33 & =A(\frac{11}{2}) \\ A & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{4x+23}{(5-2x)(x+3)}=\frac{6}{5-2x}+\frac{1}{x+3}.
$$
